answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond in the quartz ledger and declares an import batch at an island customs post. The falcon auditor recomputes its duty from the quartz duty table, using the batch manifest and value, and releases the bond on a match. Duty rises with island imports: the first batch pays 20, the k-th pays 20+6(k-1), so the 1,000th pays 6,014 and 1,000 fakes pay 3,017,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-batch ring fails because each manifest hash is key-bound to one identity; reuse burns bonds. An honest importer pays 20 once and recovers its bond when clean.
